clue.text: Drama staged for Bath Festival ?

parts.note: a bath calls for soap and a festival for opera, so a bathtime festival drama would combine the two words

explanation.surface: A play put on for the arts festival held in the city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English spa city with a well-known arts festival, which is the reading the surface pushes; the cryptic reading takes bath as a wash needing soap.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial broadcast drama, originally sponsored by detergent makers, hence the name.

clue.text: Speed in a smack

definitions.meaning: to go briskly, as in to bowl along at a good pace
a slap given as punishment, especially on the bottom

explanation.definitionFit: To spank along is to move quickly, and as a noun the word is a slap on the backside.

clue.text: Cheer Bill with insurance demand!

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a claim is a request for payment under an insurance policy

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a bill arriving alongside an insurance demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to applaud or hail loudly, a synonym of cheer as a verb.

clue.text: Poem about quails cooked -by a glamour girl

indicators.note: about means the poem's letters are placed round the other piece

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of quails are prepared in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A poet writes verses about cooking quail for a glamorous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like kitchen work on the birds; it is the anagram signal, and 'about' wraps the poem round the result, the scrambled birds sitting between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An odalisque was a concubine in a harem, and in paintings the word came to mean a reclining beauty.

clue.text: Texas pirate distressed the non-natives

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or shaken up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Texan buccaneer upset the foreigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Expatriates are people living outside their own country, so they are not natives of where they live.

clue.text: Vessel wrecked in 10 by a penned lamb

indicators.note: wrecked means the remaining letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, the Finnish-Russian region
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A boat was shipwrecked off a region where a lamb was kept in a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote his essays as Elia, so 'penned' means pen-named. Take ELIA out of KARELIA (10 across) to leave KAR, and 'wrecked' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's ark is the most famous vessel of all, a boat built to ride out the Flood.

clue.text: Has enclosed me with horse collars

indicators.note: enclosed means the first word surrounds the second

explanation.surface: Someone has fenced the speaker in among horse collars.
explanation.definitionFit: Hames are the two curved bars of a draught horse's harness collar.

clue.text: Or has been put to confusion, this invader

indicators.note: put to confusion means thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The invader was confounded by a choice of alternatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Horsa and his brother Hengist are said to have led the first Anglo-Saxon invasion of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsa was a legendary Saxon chief who came to conquer Kent in the fifth century.

clue.text: Repulsive sort of cocktail

parts.note: a petrol-bomb cocktail is thrown to repel attackers, named after a Soviet foreign minister

explanation.definitionFit: The improvised petrol bomb named after the Soviet minister was used to drive back tanks.

clue.text: Poles for flags?

parts.note: flags or banners are called by the same word as the upright posts that carry them

explanation.definitionFit: A standard is both a banner and an upright supporting post.

clue.text: Sounds like a floodlight first made from scrapped car

annotationWithheld.why: Sounds like a floodlight-first made from scrapped car (3,4): 'first made from scrapped car' gives ARC, but no words give LAMP; 'Sounds like' is no homophone of anything here
annotationWithheld.clue: Sounds like a floodlight first made from scrapped car

clue.text: Capek-country ?

parts.note: the Czech writer Capek's first name, with a country-like ending tacked on

explanation.definitionFit: A region spanning Finland and Russia, whose name begins with the Czech writer's given name Karel.

clue.text: Uniformly dusty in India for Tommy

definitions.text: Uniformly dusty in India for Tommy

parts.words: Uniformly dusty in India for Tommy
parts.note: the Hindi word for dust-coloured gave its name to the British soldier's uniform cloth

explanation.walkthrough: Tommy, from Tommy Atkins, is the old name for a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The dull brownish-yellow cloth of army uniforms takes its name from the Urdu for dusty.

clue.text: That out-of-work boy with the smart headgear

indicators.note: out of here means the word that sits outside the piece for work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: An unemployed lad wearing a smart hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out-of-work' reads as jobless, but it splits: 'out-of' is the container signal, with 'work' supplying the piece that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing a tall silk hat, the smart formal headgear of the past.

clue.text: Wrong headwear for the hog fair

definitions.text: Wrong headwear for the hog fair

parts.words: Wrong headwear for the hog fair
parts.note: a pig is bought in a poke, but these bonnets would be the wrong thing to take to a pig market

explanation.definitionFit: Women's bonnets with a projecting brim, popular in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Tomorrow's traffic, not today's ?

parts.note: plays on the Lewis Carroll line about this preserve being given tomorrow and yesterday but never today, plus a traffic hold-up

explanation.definitionFit: The White Queen's rule in Through the Looking-Glass and a snarl-up of cars share this word.

clue.text: Rosinante envious ? Just a shade

parts.note: Rosinante, Don Quixote's worn-out horse, is a jade
green with envy, so envious means green

explanation.surface: Is Don Quixote's horse jealous? Only slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour, the bluish-green of the gemstone.

clue.text: Mercurial uniped no sluggard on the Hispaniola

parts.note: someone who is not sluggish is quick
Long John Silver, the one-legged cook of Treasure Island

explanation.surface: A volatile one-legged man who is anything but lazy aboard the Hispaniola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the Hispaniola' pins down the uniped: the Hispaniola is the ship in Treasure Island, where Long John Silver sails.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes something changeable and lively, like the liquid metal mercury.

clue.text: Jan's are, what with cost of oil and current

definitions.text: Jan's are, what with cost of oil and current

parts.words: Jan's are, what with cost of oil and current
parts.note: January homes are freezing when fuel and electricity are too dear to heat them

explanation.definitionFit: Buildings, often underground, used to store ice before refrigeration.

clue.text: A midday plane for the China service

definitions.text: A midday plane for the China service

parts.words: A midday plane for the China service
parts.note: a flat surface for the midday meal on which the crockery is set

explanation.definitionFit: The furniture on which plates and dishes are laid for a meal.

clue.text: The wonder of a drop of water

definitions.text: The wonder of a drop of water

parts.words: The wonder of a drop of water
parts.note: a natural marvel that is a great fall of water

explanation.definitionFit: The famous falls on the US-Canada border are a natural wonder where a river plunges.

clue.text: Back the Ripper? Just .a has-been

indicators.note: back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a saw is a tool that rips wood

explanation.surface: Supporting Jack the Ripper? He is only a faded figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense that a has-been lives in: something that existed once but no longer is.

clue.text: Seen by rail, Kew somehow resembling Battle

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Seen from the railway, Kew Gardens looks rather like the town of Battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew and Battle are both English places, Battle the Sussex town named after the 1066 fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Warlike means martial or belligerent, having the character of combat.

clue.text: Thousand dollars is wagered by Sir Charles

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand dollars
taken as written
a bet that is on has been wagered

explanation.surface: A gentleman stakes a thousand dollars on a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Richardson's novel Sir Charles Grandison is named after its title character.

clue.text: Author whose tulip was last to be potted ?

definitions.text: Author whose tulip was last to be potted ?

parts.words: Author whose tulip was last to be potted ?
parts.note: the French novelist wrote The Black Tulip, about a quest to grow a black bloom

explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas wrote The Black Tulip as well as The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Gold to back 20's handle with floral embroidery

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold

indicators.note: back means the title is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the handle or title of Sir Charles Grandison in 20 across is Sir

explanation.surface: A man stakes gold on Sir Charles's handle, which is embroidered with flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a lace or embroidery of gold or silver thread.

clue.text: Wheat from a bee?

definitions.meaning: a spelling bee produces words written out letter by letter, hence past tense of spell

explanation.definitionFit: Spelt is an ancient grain, and it is also the British past tense of spell, as at a spelling bee.

clue.text: They're not flighty birds that embrace artists, doctor

indicators.note: embrace means the birds' word is wrapped round the artists

parts.note: emus are flightless birds
RAs, Royal Academicians, are artists

explanation.surface: Flightless birds hug a group of painters and a medic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not flighty' sounds like steady, but means unable to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch humanist scholar Erasmus held a doctorate of divinity and is often styled Doctor.

clue.text: Tack in three directions

parts.note: S is south, one of the compass directions
E is east, a second compass direction
W is west, the third compass direction

explanation.surface: A ship tacks one way, then another and another.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack is to stitch loosely, an act of needlework.

clue.text: Like a.three-piece borrowed from Francois

parts.note: a French phrase taken into English for things forming a matching set, as a suite of furniture

explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning forming a set, or attached as a room with its own bathroom.

clue.text: Northern cereal harvest approaches

parts.note: ears are the grain-bearing heads of cereal plants

explanation.surface: A grain harvest in the north is drawing close.
explanation.definitionFit: To near is to come closer, so it is a synonym of approaches.

clue.text: Initially-winged serpents' lair whence' we get buzzed

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: asps are venomous serpents
a nest is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A snake den first reached on wings, from which buzzing comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony of stinging insects, from which they swarm and buzz at us.
